warp.subtitle: Warp answers questions about your Bifrost data in natural language. It runs on its own model, configured here and kept separate from the providers Bifrost serves to your traffic.

warp.enableDesc: Adds the Warp panel to the dashboard. Warp reads logs, metrics and usage data on behalf of whoever asks, scoped to what that person can already see. It is early, so check its numbers against the dashboard before acting on them.
warp.disabledHint: Everything below is filled in, but Warp stays hidden until this is on.

warp.modelsDesc: The models Warp reasons with and writes answers from. The default answers unless someone picks another in the Warp panel. A capable model pays for itself here.

warp.maxModelsHint: Warp offers its default and up to {{count}} more models.
warp.behaviorDesc: How Warp samples, how far it may go per question, and how long chats are kept.
warp.temperatureHint: {{min}} to {{max}}. Lower gives more consistent answers, which suits a tool that reports numbers.
warp.reasoningHint: Only for reasoning models, and sent to every model listed above. Some providers reject an effort sent to a model without reasoning.
warp.maxIterationsHint: Query-and-reconsider rounds per answer. Each one is billed.
warp.requestTimeoutHint: Bound on one model call. Raise it for slow self-hosted models.
warp.retentionHint: Days after the last message. 0 uses the default of {{default}}. Separate from log retention.
warp.additionalInstructionsHint: Appended to Warp's built-in prompt, never replacing it. Useful for local naming conventions or team structure.
warp.additionalInstructionsPlaceholder: Costs are in USD. Team IDs map to squads in Notion.
warp.searchDesc: Warp embeds completed conversations into your vector store and uses them to find logs by meaning. Only vectors and operational metadata are stored there; conversation text stays in the log store.
warp.noEmbeddingProviders: None of the configured providers support embeddings. Add one that does - OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex or Cohere - before enabling Warp.
warp.modelPlaceholder: Search or type an embedding model...
warp.keysError: Could not load this provider's keys.
warp.namespaceHint: Change it whenever the provider, model or dimension changes.
warp.thresholdHint: 0.01 to 1, where 0.5 is unrelated and 1 is identical. Higher returns fewer, closer matches.
warp.namespaceWarning: Provider, model, or dimension changed. Choose a new namespace so incompatible vectors cannot mix.
warp.backfillDesc: Index completed conversations from an existing log window. Runs in the background, can be cancelled, and resumes safely across batches.
warp.saveFirst: Save configuration changes before starting a backfill.
warp.windowDone: This window is already fully indexed. Change the dates to backfill a different range.

logging.enableLogsDescription: Enable logging of requests and responses to a SQL database. This can add 40-60mb of overhead to the system memory.

logging.hiddenDescriptionBefore: Selected request types are still logged but excluded from Logs and Dashboard views, including counts, charts and filter options. Streaming and non-streaming types are separate. Leave empty to show every request type. Takes effect on the next request, no restart needed. Can also be set with
logging.hiddenLoadError: Unable to load hidden request types.
logging.disableContentLoggingD1: Applies to LLM, MCP, and agent logs. When enabled, only usage metadata (latency, cost, token count, status, routing IDs, etc.) is logged. Request/response content (messages, params, tool calls, and any raw provider bytes) is dropped from log records, even when
logging.disableContentLoggingD2: is on. Raw-byte send-back to callers via
logging.disableContentLoggingD3: is unaffected. Agent protocol bodies follow this setting; upstream raw captures also require Capture Raw Request and Response in Agent Gateway settings.
logging.retainContentD1: When enabled, requests with content logging disabled (via the global setting above or the
logging.retainContentD2: header) still have their full content offloaded to object storage, but the content is never shown in logs: the database row stays metadata-only and the UI/API never fetch the payload back. Content is then only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. When disabled, content for such requests is dropped entirely (current behavior).
logging.retainContentRequires: Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store in config.json.
logging.allowPerRequestContentD1: When enabled, individual requests can override the global content logging setting using the
logging.allowPerRequestContentD2: header or context key, and can opt-in to persisting raw provider bytes in logs using the
logging.allowPerRequestContentD3: header. Raw-byte storage requires content logging to be on, either globally, or via
logging.allowPerRequestContentD4: on the same request. If content logging is off, raw bytes are dropped from the log record even when
logging.allowPerRequestContentD5: . Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers; see Allow Per-Request Raw Override.
logging.allowRawOverrideD1: When enabled, individual requests can send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller using the
logging.allowRawOverrideD3: headers. Does not affect log storage; raw-byte persistence in logs is controlled by Allow Per-Request Content Storage Override.
logging.retentionDaysDescription: Number of days to retain logs in the database. Minimum is 1 day. Older logs will be automatically deleted.
logging.hideDeletedVK: Do Not Show Deleted VirtualKeys In Filters
logging.hideDeletedVKDescription: When enabled, deleted virtual keys are excluded from Virtual Keys filter options in Logs, Dashboard, and MCP Logs.
logging.loggingHeadersD1: Comma-separated list of request headers to capture in log metadata. Supports exact names and wildcard patterns (e.g.

cache.title: Local Cache
cache.subtitle: Cache responses locally with two complementary lookup paths: direct hash matching for exact replays, and semantic similarity search for related content. Send the x-bf-cache-key header to scope cached responses to a tenant or feature.
cache.requiresVectorStore: Requires a vector store to be configured and enabled in config.json.
cache.unexpectedError: An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.
cache.enableCachingDescription: Loads (or unloads) the plugin without a server restart. Configuration changes you make below mutate the live plugin in place, no redeploy needed.
cache.semanticDisabledTitle: Configure an embedding-capable provider to enable semantic mode.
cache.modeDirectDesc: Direct-only mode hashes each request and replays an exact match. No embeddings, no provider needed. Cheapest path, perfect for stable prompts.
cache.modeSemanticDesc: Direct + semantic mode adds vector similarity search on top of direct hash matching. Requires an embedding-capable provider and the model's real dimension. Direct hits are still served first; semantic search runs only when the direct lookup misses.
cache.headsUp: Heads up: a vector store namespace can only hold vectors of one dimension. Whenever you change the embedding provider, model, or dimension, make sure the dimension still matches what the model produces, otherwise writes to the existing namespace will fail and reads will silently miss. The namespace is not recreated automatically; either use a fresh namespace or drop the existing class/index in your vector store before saving.
cache.modelPlaceholder: Search or type an embedding model...
cache.apiKeyNote: API keys are inherited from the embedding provider's main configuration, you don't need to add them again here.
cache.dimensionHint: Vector size produced by the embedding model. Must match the model exactly (e.g. 1536 for OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 3072 for text-embedding-3-large, 768 for many Cohere/Voyage models).
cache.ttlHint: How long cached entries live before they expire. Override per-request via the x-bf-cache-ttl header.
cache.thresholdHint: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit. Override per-request via x-bf-cache-threshold.
cache.nsHint: Bucket/index name where cache entries live. Leave blank to use the default (BifrostLocalCachePlugin). Changing this points the plugin at a different (possibly empty) bucket. Old entries are not deleted, they just stop being queried.
cache.ckHint: Fallback partition key used when a request doesn't set x-bf-cache-key. Cache keys isolate entries: same key ↔ shared cache pool. Leave blank to disable caching for any request that doesn't send the header.
cache.historyHint: Skip caching for conversations with more than this many messages. Long histories rarely match exactly and inflate the cache without paying off.
cache.excludeSystemHint: Strip system messages from the cache key.
cache.cacheByModelHint: Include model name in the cache key. Different models won't share cached responses.
cache.cacheByProviderHint: Include provider name in the cache key. Different providers won't share cached responses.
cache.scopeIdentityHint: Serve a cached response only to the virtual key and user that wrote it. Turn off to share entries across identities that send the same cache key.
cache.overrideKey: x-bf-cache-key: scope this request to a specific cache partition.
cache.overrideTtl: x-bf-cache-ttl: override TTL for just this request.
cache.overrideType: x-bf-cache-type: send direct or semantic to limit lookup to one path.
cache.overrideNoStore: x-bf-cache-no-store: true to skip writing the response (still serves cached hits).

mcp.title: MCP Settings
mcp.subtitle: Configure MCP (Model Context Protocol) agent and tool settings.
mcp.agentDepthPositive: Max agent depth must be a positive number.
mcp.toolTimeoutPositive: Tool execution timeout must be a positive number.
mcp.syncIntervalNonNeg: Tool sync interval must be zero or a positive number.
mcp.perClientNonNeg: Max instruction length per server must be zero or a positive number.
mcp.totalNonNeg: Max instruction length total must be zero or a positive number.
mcp.authCodeTtlRange: Authorization code TTL must be between 1 and 900 seconds (15 minutes).
mcp.accessTokenTtlMin: Access token TTL must be at least 60 seconds.
mcp.maxAgentDepthDesc: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcp.toolTimeoutDesc: Maximum time in seconds for tool execution.
mcp.syncIntervalDesc: How often to refresh tool lists from MCP servers. Set to 0 to use the default of 10 minutes.
mcp.tempTokenDesc: When enabled, per-user MCP OAuth links can include a short-lived scoped token so someone without an active Bifrost dashboard session can complete the flow. Keep disabled to require normal dashboard authentication.
mcp.maxInstrPerServerDesc: Longer text is truncated with a notice. Set to 0 to use the default of 4096.
mcp.bindingLevelDesc: How tools are exposed in the VFS: server-level (all tools per server) or tool-level (individual tools).
mcp.vfsServerNote: All tools per server in a single .py file
mcp.externalUrlDesc: Override Bifrost's public base URL when it runs behind a reverse proxy. Leave blank to derive the URL from the incoming Host header. Used as the redirect_uri Bifrost registers with upstream OAuth providers when it acts as a client to an MCP server (e.g. Notion or Jira redirect the browser to <URL>/api/oauth/callback after login). Supports env var syntax (e.g. env.BIFROST_EXTERNAL_URL).
mcp.redirectWarningTitle: Changing this URL can break existing MCP clients
mcp.redirectWarningBody: Upstream OAuth providers lock the redirect_uri to whatever was registered initially, so MCP clients that already completed OAuth will fail with "Invalid redirect URI". To recover, clear the stored OAuth client credentials for the affected MCP servers and re-authorize so Bifrost re-runs Dynamic Client Registration with the new URL.
mcp.authModeDesc: Controls how inbound MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) authenticate to the /mcp endpoint. headers (default) - VK / api-key / session headers only, OAuth discovery disabled. both - accepts header credentials and Bifrost-issued JWTs; existing integrations are unaffected. oauth - JWTs only; VK and header access is disabled.
mcp.oauthModeWarningTitle: VK / header MCP access will be disabled
mcp.oauthModeWarningBody: All existing MCP integrations that use a virtual key, api-key, or session header will stop working immediately. Clients must re-authenticate via the OAuth consent flow to obtain a JWT before they can connect.
mcp.headersModeWarningBody: All MCP clients that authenticated via the OAuth consent flow will lose access; their JWTs will be rejected and their refresh tokens will become unusable. They will need to reconfigure using a virtual key or api-key header.
mcp.bothModeNote: Existing VK / header integrations continue to work unchanged. New MCP clients can connect via OAuth - they'll be redirected to the consent page to pick an identity.
mcp.issuerUrlDesc: Stable public URL advertised in discovery documents and embedded as the iss claim in every JWT. Leave blank to derive it from the request Host header (sufficient for most deployments). Multi-host or reverse-proxy deployments might need this. Supports env var syntax (e.g. env.BIFROST_ISSUER_URL).
mcp.authCodeTtlDesc: How long the one-time code is valid after the consent page redirects back to the MCP client (default: 300, max 900 = 15 min).
mcp.accessTokenTtlDesc: Lifetime of issued JWT Bearer tokens. Clients silently refresh when expired (default: 600 = 10 min). Also bounds how long a revoked grant keeps working before it is cut off.
mcp.requireIdpDesc: When enabled, the OAuth consent flow only offers identity-provider login. Virtual keys can no longer be used to obtain an MCP token, and existing virtual-key OAuth sessions lose access immediately. Anonymous session access is unaffected (controlled by Enforce Authentication on Inference).
mcp.vkStopTitle: Virtual-key MCP access via OAuth will stop
mcp.vkStopBody: MCP clients that authenticated with a virtual key will lose access immediately and must sign in through your identity provider to reconnect.

codeMode.title: Code Mode Limits
codeMode.description: Limits on each code execution. Leave a field empty to use its default. Executions are not limited in how many run at once.

max_source_bytes.label: Max Source Size (bytes)
max_source_bytes.desc: Largest code a single execution may submit.

max_steps.label: Max Computation Steps
max_steps.desc: Interpreter steps per execution, including work inside builtins.

max_memory_bytes.label: Max Memory (bytes)
max_memory_bytes.desc: Estimated allocation budget per execution. Every concurrent execution gets its own budget.

max_log_bytes.label: Max Log Output (bytes)
max_log_bytes.desc: Print and tool log output per execution, including newlines.

max_tool_calls.label: Max Tool Calls
max_tool_calls.desc: Nested MCP tool calls per execution.

max_value_bytes.label: Max Value Size (bytes)
max_value_bytes.desc: Size budget for each tool payload and converted result. Must be at least 1024.

max_nesting_depth.label: Max Nesting Depth
max_nesting_depth.desc: Nesting depth of values crossing the tool boundary. At most 1000.

codeMode.valueMin: Max value size must be at least {{min}} bytes.
codeMode.depthMax: Max nesting depth must be at most {{max}}.

mcp.disableAutoInjectDescPre: When enabled, MCP tools are not automatically included in every request. Tools are only injected when explicitly specified via request headers (
mcp.disableAutoInjectDescPost: ) and still must be allowed by the virtual key MCP configuration.
mcp.maxInstrTotalDescPre: Ceiling across every server a caller can see. At
mcp.maxInstrTotalDescPost: this rides on every MCP-bearing request, so raising it raises per-request tokens. Set to 0 to use the default of 16384.
mcp.blockedHostsPlaceholder: Add host, IP, or CIDR (Enter or comma)

security.title: Security Settings
security.subtitle: Configure security and access control settings.
security.invalidOrigins: Invalid origins: {{origins}}. Origins must be valid URLs like https://example.com, wildcard patterns like https://*.example.com, or "*" to allow all origins
security.cooldownInvalid: Rotation cooldown must be a duration like "30s", "5m", or "1h30m" (leave empty to disable).
security.setupTokenRequired: Enter the setup token configured by your operator to create the first admin account. It's set via setup_token in config.json or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable.
security.proofFallback: Confirm this change with the current admin password or a setup token.
security.authTypeError: Could not load authentication type. Dashboard password settings are hidden until this request succeeds. {{message}}
security.passwordProtectDesc: Set up authentication credentials to protect your Bifrost dashboard. Once configured, use the generated token for all admin API calls.
security.passwordHint: Use at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Env var references are accepted.
security.currentPasswordPlaceholder: Enter the admin password currently in use
security.confirmHint: Dashboard protection is switched off, so this session is not signed in. Turning it back on or changing the admin credentials requires the admin password that is currently stored.
security.confirmWithSetupToken: ...or confirm with a setup token instead
security.setupTokenPlaceholder: Paste the setup token configured by your operator
security.setupTokenAltHint: If the current password is not at hand, the setup_token from config.json (or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable) confirms this change too.
security.setupAuthorized: Authorized with the setup token entered on the setup screen. Saving creates the admin account, after which the setup token stops working.
security.setupTokenHint: No admin account exists yet, so management APIs only accept the setup token. Enter the token configured via setup_token in config.json (or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable) to create the admin account. Once it is enabled, the setup token stops working.
security.enforceInferenceDescEnt: Require authentication (virtual key, API key, or user token) for all inference endpoints.
security.enforceInferenceDescOss: Require a virtual key for all inference requests.
security.enforceInferenceTail: to set up a virtual key before enabling this. Calls without a valid credential will return 401.
security.inferenceWarning: The dashboard is authentication protected, but this is a separate control: anyone who can reach this gateway can still call inference endpoints (e.g. chat completions) with no credential at all, spending your provider budget and reading provider-side state your key has access to. Turn this on unless you've deliberately chosen to leave inference open.
security.dualCredentialDesc: How to handle inference requests that present both an identity provider access token (Authorization: Bearer) and a virtual key (x-bf-vk). Prefer IDP token uses the user token for identity, Prefer virtual key drops the IDP token and authenticates via the virtual key, and Reject request returns a 400 error.
security.allowDirectKeysDesc: When enabled, callers can pass a provider API key directly in the Authorization, x-api-key, or x-goog-api-key header alongside x-bf-direct-key: true. Bifrost will use that key directly, bypassing the registered key pool.
security.rotationCooldownDesc: After rotating a virtual key, the previous value keeps authenticating for this long, giving callers time to switch to the new key. Use a duration like 30s, 5m, or 1h. Leave empty (or 0) to have the old value stop working immediately. Maximum 30 days.
security.deleteExpiredDesc: When enabled, a daily cleanup job deletes every virtual key whose expiry has passed and posts a notification listing the removed keys. Each key can override this from its Delete after expire switch: a key set to off is kept, and a key set to on is deleted even while this is disabled.
security.allowedOriginsDesc: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS and WebSocket connections. Localhost origins are always allowed. Each origin must be a complete URL with protocol (e.g., https://app.example.com, http://10.0.0.100:3000). Wildcards are supported for subdomains (e.g., https://*.example.com) or use "*" to allow all origins.
security.allowedHeadersDesc: Comma-separated list of allowed headers for CORS.
security.requiredHeadersDesc: Comma-separated list of headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers will be rejected with a 400 error. Header names are case-insensitive.
security.whitelistedRoutesDesc: Comma-separated list of routes that bypass the auth middleware. Requests to these routes will not require authentication. System routes like /health, /api/session/login, and /api/session/is-auth-enabled are always whitelisted regardless of this setting.

pprof.subtitle: Development only - Runtime profiling and memory analysis
